Get started with mintyrasr

Source: vignettes/mintyrasr.Rmd
mintyrasr.Rmd

中文版

ASReml-R is licensed software, so the code on this page is not run when the site is built. Every chunk runs as shown on a computer with ASReml-R 4.

What the package does

mintyr prepares the data for the usual comparison of genomic prediction models: for every scenario a nested table for parameter estimation (all records) and a table of training / validation sets (one row per repeat x fold), all validated on the same individuals. mintyrasr takes both tables and, for every row:

  1. fits the model to the full data: variance components, h2 and, for two traits, rg, rp and an LRT of rg = 0;
  2. refits it to every training set (variance components fixed, warm-started or re-estimated);
  3. predicts the GEBVs of the validation individuals and computes their reliability, the predictive ability, the accuracy and the slope;
  4. summarises over folds and writes one Excel workbook per scenario.
function use
asr_gblup(param, cv, ginv, ...) one scenario (or any nested table + CV table)
asr_scenarios(sc, ginv, ...) all scenarios of mintyr::cv_scenarios() in one call

Installation 

# ASReml-R 4 must be installed and licensed first (https://vsni.co.uk/)
install.packages("mintyr")
pak::pak("tony2015116/mintyrasr")

1. Prepare the inputs

You need three objects:

  • phenotypes: one row per individual, with the ID, the grouping column (herd, line, …), fixed effects and the traits;
  • ginv: the inverse genomic relationship matrix in a form vm() accepts. It must carry attr(ginv, "INVERSE") <- TRUE, otherwise vm() treats it as G itself (mintyrasr warns);
  • inbreeding (optional): a data.frame (id, F) for the reliability 1 - PEV / ((1 + F) Va). For GBLUP, F = diag(G) - 1 is common. Without it, F = 0 is used.
library(asreml)
library(ASRgenomics)
library(mintyr)
library(mintyrasr)

pheno <- import_xlsx("pheno.xlsx")             # id, test_herd, hhys, adg, bf, fcr

G    <- G.matrix(M = snp, method = "VanRaden")$G
ginv <- G.inverse(G = G, sparseform = TRUE)$Ginv.sparse   # carries INVERSE = TRUE
inbreeding <- data.frame(id = rownames(G), F = diag(G) - 1)

2. Build the scenarios with mintyr 

sc <- cv_scenarios(pheno, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr"), id = "id",
                   group = "test_herd", v = 5, repeats = 5, seed = 2026,
                   out_type = "df")      # ASReml-R needs data.frames
sc
scenario model parameter data training set
st_sp single-trait, single group trait x group target group
st_mp single-trait, groups combined trait target group + all other groups
mt_sp two-trait, single group trait pair x group target group
mt_mp two-trait, groups combined trait pair target group + all other groups
mt_bt one trait as a different trait in each group trait target group + all other groups

3. Run all scenarios 

res <- asr_scenarios(sc, ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, inbreeding = inbreeding,
                     dir = "results")
# results/st_sp_ginv.xlsx, st_mp_ginv.xlsx, mt_sp_ginv.xlsx, mt_mp_ginv.xlsx

res$st_sp$summary
res$mt_sp$param

Add "mt_bt" to scenarios for one trait treated as a different trait in each of two groups (G x E). It is fitted with a diag residual and without rp, because no individual has records in both groups:

res_bt <- asr_scenarios(sc, ginv, scenarios = "mt_bt", fixed = ~ hhys,
                        genetic_cov = "corgh", inbreeding = inbreeding)
res_bt$mt_bt$param        # h2 per group, rg between groups (+ SE), rg_p

4. One scenario at a time

asr_gblup() takes a nested parameter table and a CV table. They are matched through their shared outer columns (name, pairs, test_herd, …).

st <- asr_gblup(sc$st_sp$param, sc$st_sp$cv, ginv = ginv,
                fixed = ~ hhys, inbreeding = inbreeding,
                path = "results/st_sp_ginv.xlsx")
st

Tables built by hand with w2l_nest() / c2p_nest() + nest_cv() work too. When the response columns are not called value / value1 + value2, name them in traits:

nested <- w2l_nest(pheno, cols = c("adg", "bf"), by = "test_herd", out_type = "df")
cvtab  <- nest_cv(nested, v = 5, repeats = 2, seed = 1, out_type = "df")
asr_gblup(nested, cvtab, ginv, fixed = ~ hhys)

asr_gblup(all_nest5, all_cv5, ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, traits = c("bfs", "nls"),
          genetic_cov = "corgh", residual_cov = "diag", rp = FALSE)

5. What you get

Each result is a list; every element becomes one sheet of the workbook.

element content
varcomp summary(fit)$varcomp of every parameter fit, with its V number
vc_index which V is which component: term, role (genetic / random / residual), kind (var / cov / cor), traits, used
param h2 (two traits: per trait), rg, rp with SE; formulas used; status, converge, updates, iterations, loglik, boundary; rg_lrt, rg_p (and cov_* with test_rp = TRUE)
accuracy per repeat x fold x trait: status, n, pa, accuracy, slope, va, h2_full, cv_converge, cv_updates, cv_iter
summary pa, accuracy, slope: n, mean, sd, se over the folds with status == "ok"
pred validation individuals: obs, gebv, pev, inb (F), rel
gebv all individuals of the full-data fit: gebv, pev, inb, rel, reliable
log every error, non-convergence, boundary estimate and invalid LRT, with time and label
  • pa (predictive ability) = r(y, GEBV) on the validation individuals;
  • accuracy = pa / sqrt(h2), with h2 from the full data (Dekkers 2007);
  • slope = b(y ~ GEBV); 1 means no inflation or deflation of the GEBVs.

Reliability in cross-validation is not filtered (cv_min_rel = -Inf). Validation individuals have no record of their own in the training set, so a low reliability is expected; keeping only the high-reliability ones would bias PA towards well-connected individuals and shrink the sample. The threshold min_rel (default 0.05) is applied to the final GEBVs of the full-data fit instead, as the flag gebv$reliable. A fold needs at least min_n (default 10) validation individuals, otherwise its PA, accuracy and slope are NA. Negative values are kept (neg_to_na = FALSE): dropping them would bias the mean upwards.

6. Variance components in cross-validation

cv_vc in each fold note
"fixed" (default) fixed at the full-data estimates (Constraint = "F", maxit = 1) fastest; slight leakage, because the validation records were used to estimate them
"warm" re-estimated from the training set, starting from the full-data values
"estimate" re-estimated from default start values no leakage; slowest

The va used for the reliability is always taken from the model of that fold.

7. Long runs: progress, update() and safe running

One line per fit shows the status, iterations, time and the estimated time left; ASReml’s own iteration monitor is switched off while mintyrasr runs (asreml_trace = TRUE to see it):

asr_gblup: two-trait model | 4 parameter fit(s) + 60 CV fit(s) | cv_vc = "fixed"
[param 1/4] pairs=adg-bf test_herd=nls | ok | 9 it, 21s
[param 2/4] pairs=adg-bf test_herd=bfs | ok after 1 update() | 31 it, 48s
[cv 12/60  20%] pairs=adg-bf test_herd=nls rep=Repeat2 fold=Fold2 | ok | 2 it, 4s | 6.1 min elapsed, ~19.5 min left
Done in 31.2 min | param: 4 ok, 0 not converged, 0 failed | cv: ok 60 | 1 log entry
  • update(): a fit that has not converged is continued from its current estimates up to max_update = 2 times (param$updates, accuracy$cv_updates).
  • Not converged after that (nonconv = "skip", default): a parameter fit is reported with status = "not_converged" and its CV rows are skipped (status = "param_not_converged"); a CV fit gives NA for its fold. nonconv = "keep" uses such fits anyway.
  • Errors: a failing fit gets status = "failed", the loop carries on (on_error = "stop" to stop at once).
  • $log records every error, non-convergence, boundary estimate and invalid LRT with time, stage and label; one warning at the end says how many fits failed or did not converge.
  • Rows with a status other than "ok" are left out of summary.

Other notes:

  • Fitted models are not kept: memory stays low even with many folds.
  • workspace = "auto" sizes ASReml’s workspace from the number of individuals and traits. ASReml reserves the whole workspace for every fit, so a large fixed value (e.g. "30Gb") slows every fit down - and on a 32 GB computer can run out of memory. maxit = 100 (ASReml’s default is 13).
  • na_x = "include" (default, as in many scripts) treats missing covariates as 0 - centre numeric covariates first. ASReml’s own default is "fail".
  • Further asreml() arguments: asreml_args = list(ai.sing = TRUE).
  • Keep the computer awake during long runs: a sleeping computer (or an online licence waiting) shows up as a long pause, not as slow fitting.
